author: Procopius of Gaza
occasion: Procopius refutes chapter 140 of Proclus's Elements of Theology, defending the Christian doctrine of the Trinity and creation against Neoplatonic emanation.
argument: Procopius argues that the only unoriginate and endless divine procession is the generation of the Son and the procession of the Holy Spirit from the Father alone, which constitutes the Trinity without departing from the Father's essence. All other processions belong to things that have come into being from the Father through the Son and are completed in the Spirit. Among these, the processions of eternal things according to essence are completed, while those according to illumination proceed perpetually in ordered ranks, and all things return to the one origin in an eternal cycle. The procession of things subject to generation, corruption, and time was completed in its universal aspect when the sensible world was finished in six days, though particular works continue until the common consummation. At that consummation a final procession will transform all things from corruption to incorruption, and God will be all in all.

outline.move: Introduces the refutation of Proclus's 140th theological chapter and states that the only unoriginate and endless divine procession is the generation of the Son and the procession of the Holy Spirit from the Father alone, forming the Trinity, as Gregory the Theologian says.

Explains that this divine procession alone has the Father as unoriginate beginning, the Son as co-originate middle, and the Holy Spirit as super-perfect end, and that it does not depart from the Father's essence, unlike all other processions of beings.

Distinguishes the processions of eternal things: those according to essence are completed, while those according to illumination proceed perpetually from there in ordered ranks; and all things return to the one origin in an eternal cycle.

States that the sensible world was completed in six days, particular works continue until the common consummation, and then a final procession will transform all things from corruption to incorruption, with God all in all.

cast.name: Procopius of Gaza
cast.who: Christian rhetorician and biblical commentator writing against Proclus.

cast.name: Proclus
cast.who: Neoplatonic philosopher whose theological chapters are being refuted.

cast.name: Gregory the Theologian
cast.who: Gregory of Nazianzus, cited as authority for the Trinity.

cast.name: The Savior
cast.who: Jesus Christ, quoted as speaker in the Gospel of John.

voices.speaker: Gregory the Theologian
voices.how_marked: Introduced by 'καθάπερ φησιν ὁ ἡμέτερος Θεολόγος Γρηγόριος' (as our Theologian Gregory says).

voices.speaker: The Savior (Jesus)
voices.how_marked: Introduced by 'καθὰ εἴρηται τῷ Σωτῆρι' (as was said by the Savior) and quoted directly.

key_terms.sense: Procession or going forth from a source; the central concept being distinguished between divine and created.
Without beginning or origin; applied to the Father and the divine procession.
Without end; applied to the divine procession and some created processions.
The Father as the single source or unit from which the Trinity proceeds.
The pair of Son and Spirit as the Father moves into duality.
The Trinity of Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.
Illumination or shining forth; a kind of procession of eternal things that is perpetual.
Return or turning back to the origin; the movement of all things toward God.
The final transformation of all things from corruption to incorruption.
Radiance or effulgence; divine illuminations poured out in ordered ranks.

scripture: The author cites the Gospel of John 5:17 ('My Father is working until now, and I am working') and alludes to Genesis 1–2 (six days of creation, seventh-day rest) and 1 Corinthians 15:28 ('God all in all'). LXX book names and Psalm numbering are not explicitly used in this fragment.
uncertain: The exact date of composition within Procopius's lifetime.
The precise extent of the original work, since only a fragment survives.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Gregory the Theologian: 'Gregory of Nazianzus, cited as authority for the Trinity.'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: καθάπερ φησιν ὁ ἡμέτερος Θεολόγος Γρηγόριος
_unresolved_facts.fix: Gregory of Nazianzus, cited as authority that the monad moved to a dyad and stopped at the Trinity (τὴν ἐν Υἱῷ θεωρουμένην καὶ Πνεύματι, μέχρι Τριάδος ἔστη)

_unresolved_facts.claim: u01-rem-early move: 'and that it does not depart from the Father's essence, unlike all other processions of beings.'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: οὐδὲ γὰρ ἐξίστησιν ὅλως τῆς ἀρχῆς τὰ ἐξ αὐτῆς, ἀλλ' ἀνεκφοίτητα πάντη ταύτης τηρεῖ, διὰ τὴν τῆς οὐσίας ταυτότητα
_unresolved_facts.fix: and that it does not depart from the origin at all but preserves things as not going forth from it entirely, due to the identity of essence; unlike all other processions of beings which are divided together with beings

_unresolved_facts.claim: u01-rem-mid move: 'and all things return to the one origin in an eternal cycle.'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: οὕτω δὲ καὶ πάντα πρὸς τὴν μίαν ἀρχὴν ἀνατατικῶς ἐπιστρέφει· καὶ ὁ ἀΐδιος τούτοις καὶ ἀτελεύτητος ἔν τε ταῖς προόδοις καὶ ταῖς ἐπιτροφαῖς κύκλος σώζεται
_unresolved_facts.fix: and all things return to the one origin in an upward-tending manner; and for these things the eternal and endless cycle is preserved both in processions and in returns (ἐπιστροφαῖς, not ἐπιτροφαῖς)

_unresolved_facts.claim: All other processions belong to things that have come into being from the Father through the Son and are completed in the Spirit.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: πάντα γέγονε παρὰ τοῦ Πατρὸς διὰ τοῦ Υἱοῦ συντελεσθέντα τῷ Πνεύματι
_unresolved_facts.fix: All things came to be from the Father through the Son, having been completed by the Spirit (συντελεσθέντα τῷ Πνεύματι = completed by/with the Spirit, not 'in' the Spirit as a location)

_unresolved_facts.claim: those according to illumination proceed perpetually in ordered ranks
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: τοῖς μὲν πρωτοδότως, τοῖς δὲ δευτεροδότως, καὶ καθεξῆς
_unresolved_facts.fix: those according to illumination proceed perpetually from there, for some in a first-given manner, for others in a second-given manner, and so on in sequence

_unresolved_facts.claim: At that consummation a final procession will transform all things from corruption to incorruption
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: καὶ ἄλλη τηνικαῦτα πρόοδος ἔσται, καθ' ἣν ἔσται ὁ Θεὸς τὰ πάντα ἐν πᾶσιν
_unresolved_facts.fix: At that consummation there will be another procession, according to which God will be all in all; and the trans-elementation of all things and transformation from corruption to incorruption

_unresolved_facts.claim: The Savior (Jesus): 'Introduced by 'καθὰ εἴρηται τῷ Σωτῆρι' (as was said by the Savior) and quoted directly.'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: καθὰ εἴρηται τῷ Σωτῆρι· "ὁ Πατήρ μου ἕως ἄρτι ἐργάζεται, κἀγὼ ἐργάζομαι"
_unresolved_facts.fix: Introduced by 'καθὰ εἴρηται τῷ Σωτῆρι' (as was said to the Savior) — dative of person addressed, not 'by the Savior'; Jesus is the one who speaks the quoted words, not the one addressed
